proposition: There is a tension of emphasis between the Prologue's picture of Ibn Turka refusing to bend the knee at his inquisitions and the dissertation's picture of two apologies addressed to Shāhrukh and Bāysunghur: the first defends Sufism as within the Sunna, attacks his accusers and presents him as a standard Ashʿari in the companion creed; the second pleads at length for Bāysunghur's mediation. Neither page says the two accounts are the same event seen from different sides; this is a difference of characterisation the game should not resolve.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I/II, as reported by Melvin-Koushki
mediation.note: written to the rulers judging him; the dissertation calls the apologies the primary source for his life (pdf 75)
